title: Interview Practice Study
body1:
You are invited to participate in a research study evaluating an AI-assisted behavioral interview tool. Your participation will involve answering interview questions with an AI coach and completing brief surveys about your experience. The entire session takes approximately 25–30 minutes.

Your participation is completely voluntary. You may stop or skip any question at any time without penalty. All responses collected are confidential and used solely for research purposes.

Your chat messages and survey answers will be recorded. We do not collect your name, so please do not include names or other identifying details in your answers.

Interview practice, including receiving feedback on your answers, can be mildly stressful for some people. If you feel uncomfortable at any point, you may stop the session by closing this window.

header: Thank You for participating in the study.
body1:
Thank you for taking part. To get natural reactions, we did not tell you the full purpose of this study at the start. Our research is about how the tone of an AI interviewer's feedback affects people's confidence. Each person was randomly assigned to one of three interviewer styles: supportive, neutral, or passive-aggressive. The interview questions and the main points of the feedback were the same in all three styles. Only the tone changed.

We set the AI interviewer's tone ahead of time. It was not a judgment of you or of your answers. We are comparing how confident people feel before and after the practice interview in each group.

To help make sure other participants respond naturally, please do not share details of this study with others.

Taking part is still voluntary. Now that you know the full purpose, you may choose to have your data removed, without penalty. To do this, email [[CONTACT NAME AND EMAIL]] within [[NUMBER]] days and include your access code. After that, we will not be able to identify your data to remove it.

Questions? Please contact [[CONTACT NAME AND EMAIL]]. If you have questions or concerns about your rights as a research participant, you can contact the Carnegie Mellon IRB at (412) 268-4721, IRB-review@andrew.cmu.edu.
